findings.claim: The --due, --no-due and --priority success tests run only on bare tasks, so nothing checks that these edits leave the task's other keys (tags, title, done, id) and other tasks untouched.
findings.failure_scenario: An edit_task that rebuilds the dict on --priority/--due, or drops tags when it deletes a key, passes every success test. A task with tags and a due date loses its tags on `edit 1 --priority normal` and no test fails. Only the --title test uses a full task.

findings.claim: The core no-mutation test pairs a valid title with each bad value, so it never catches a partial edit where a valid priority or due is applied before a later field fails. It also never tests a combined successful edit.
findings.failure_scenario: edit_task validates the title first, applies priority, then validates due. `edit_task(tasks, 1, priority='low', due='nope')` raises after mutating priority. The CLI tests cannot see this because the file is not saved on error. The core test never uses priority with a bad due, so it passes.
